The filing also updates Rule 19.3(i)(1) to permit listing of options on ETFs as defined under Rule 6c-11 and removes product-specific references. This expands the eligible underlying universe for BZX options, with immediate effectiveness.

rationale: This is a Cboe BYX (equities) rule filing introducing a Data Vendor definition and fee-waiver program for Cboe One Summary/Premium feeds. It is a fee/market-data distribution matter, not a protocol, order-type, connectivity, or certification change relevant to options market-making infrastructure.

LTSE rule change amending Clearly Erroneous Execution rules to align with newly approved Overnight Protected Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. This is a structural rule filing affecting how executions are reviewed during overnight sessions, relevant to market-structure direction but on a lower-priority equity-only venue.
summary: LTSE amended Rule 11.270 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) following the SEC's August 5, 2026 approval of LULD Plan Amendment 27, which establishes temporary static Overnight Price Bands of 20% above and below two reference points for 23/5 trading. The change extends the rule's premise—that executions within available and correct LULD Price Bands are not eligible for clearly erroneous review—to overnight sessions where bands were previously unavailable.

rationale: Rule filing amending ISE's Market-Wide Speed Bump and Kill Switch to remove cross-market functionality with GEMX, harmonizing with MRX/Phlx/NTX/NOM per-exchange-only behavior. This is a structural rule change affecting market-maker risk controls and order-entry protocols (FIX, OTTO, Precise), directly relevant to options market-making infrastructure.
summary: Nasdaq ISE filed to amend Options 3, Section 15(a)(3)(B)(vii) (Market-Wide Speed Bump) and Options 3, Section 17 (Kill Switch) to eliminate cross-market functionality between ISE and Nasdaq GEMX. Currently, ISE market makers can configure the MWSB parameter and Kill Switch to apply across both ISE and GEMX; the proposal removes that election, making both protections per-exchange only, consistent with MRX, Phlx, NTX Options, and NOM. Members using cross-market MWSB or Kill Switch configurations on ISE/GEMX will need to adjust their risk-control setups accordingly.

rationale: This is a Cboe EDGX rule filing introducing a Data Vendor program with fee waivers for market data distribution; it is a routine fee/membership matter rather than a protocol, order-type, or connectivity change.
summary: Cboe EDGX filed to introduce a Data Vendor definition and program that waives External Distribution Fees for Data Vendors redistributing the Cboe One Summary, Cboe One Premium, EDGX Summary Depth, and EDGX Top feeds. The filing also codifies the existing Extranet Service Provider definition and an existing practice limiting liability for dual Cboe One Summary/Premium distributors to the Premium fee. No technical or connectivity changes are described.

rationale: Rule change alters PRIME/cPRIME auction RFR message handling: instead of rejecting responses priced worse than the initiating price, the System will process them and send a cancellation at auction conclusion. This is a protocol/behavior change for options auction connectivity and order handling on MIAX.
summary: MIAX is amending Rule 515A(a)(2)(i)(D) so that PRIME and cPRIME Auction RFR responses submitted at a price not equal to or better than the initiating price are no longer rejected on receipt; the System will process the message and issue a cancellation message at the conclusion of the Auction. Filed as immediately effective, so member systems handling PRIME/cPRIME auction responses should expect the new accept-then-cancel behavior rather than an immediate reject.

rationale: Nasdaq Texas rule filing amending Clearly Erroneous Transaction rules to align with newly approved Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. This is a structural rule change affecting error-trade review during overnight sessions, relevant to market-structure direction but not a protocol/spec or connectivity change.
summary: Nasdaq Texas is amending Equity 11, Rule 11890 (Clearly Erroneous Transactions) to extend the restriction on clearly erroneous review to overnight trading hours, following the SEC's August 5, 2026 approval of Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. The current rule bars CEE review during Market Hours when LULD bands are available; the amendment extends this logic to overnight sessions where temporary static bands 20% above/below two reference points will apply.

rationale: A Nasdaq Texas rule filing eliminating redundant information-circular distribution for UTP derivative securities and updating cross-references; it is a structural rule change but has no protocol, connectivity, or certification impact for options market-making infrastructure.

PHLX rule filing amending Clearly Erroneous Transaction rules to align with newly approved Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading; structurally notable for market-making operations but not a protocol/spec or connectivity change.
summary: Nasdaq PHLX filed to amend Equity 4, Rule 3312 (Clearly Erroneous Transactions) to extend the restriction on clearly erroneous review to overnight trading hours, following the SEC's August 5, 2026 approval of Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 Trading. The current rule bars CEE review during Market Hours when LULD bands are available; the amendment extends this treatment to the overnight session where temporary static bands of 20% above/below two reference points will apply.

rationale: Routine fee schedule amendment adding IEX to an existing routing fee code (RP) at the same $0.25/contract rate; no protocol, order-type, or connectivity impact.

SEC extension of the review period for a CMESC cross-margin rule change with CME; it is a clearing/margin structural filing, not an options-market protocol or venue change, and the November 29 date is the Commission's action deadline rather than a deadline for the reader's systems.

Cboe proposes new session-eligibility order instructions ('GTH Only' and 'GTH and RTH Only') under Rule 5.6(c), plus earlier order acceptance and Curb availability on shortened days — directly affecting order-entry protocol and session handling for options market-making systems.
summary: Cboe is amending Rule 5.6(c) to add two new session instructions: 'GTH Only' (eligible solely during Global Trading Hours; unexecuted Day orders cancelled at GTH close) and 'GTH and RTH Only' (excludes Curb). The filing also provides for earlier order acceptance times and makes Curb sessions available on shortened/half-day trading days, aligning with NYSE American and Nasdaq MRX rules. These changes affect order-entry session designation logic and GTH/Curb eligibility handling.

rationale: EDGX proposes to amend Rule 11.15 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) to align with the SEC-approved Overnight Protected Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading, extending CEE review restrictions to overnight sessions. This is a structural rule filing affecting execution/cancellation logic, though it is an immediately effective notice with no stated compliance deadline.
summary: Cboe EDGX filed to amend Rule 11.15 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) in response to the SEC's August 5, 2026 approval of Overnight Protected Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. The change extends the rule's premise—that trades within available and correct LULD Price Bands are not eligible for clearly erroneous review—to overnight trading hours, where bands were previously unavailable. The filing is immediately effective; no certification or cutover date is stated.

rationale: Cboe BZX rule filing amending Clearly Erroneous Execution review to align with newly approved Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. summary: Cboe BZX filed to amend Rule 11.17 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) following the SEC's August 5, 2026 approval of Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. The change extends the principle that executions within available and correct LULD bands are not eligible for clearly erroneous review into overnight sessions, where bands were previously unavailable. This alters the error-trade cancellation framework for overnight trading.

rationale: Amendment to Cboe BYX Rule 11.17 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) to align with newly approved Overnight Price Bands under the LULD Plan for 23/5 trading. This is a structural rule filing affecting trade-break/review mechanics, relevant to market-structure direction but not a protocol or connectivity change.
summary: Cboe BYX is amending Rule 11.17 (Clearly Erroneous Executions) to account for Overnight Price Bands approved under LULD Plan Amendment 27 on August 5, 2026, which established temporary static bands 20% above/below two reference points during overnight trading. The current rule bars clearly-erroneous review when LULD Price Bands were available and correct, but that restriction has applied only during Regular Trading Hours; the amendment extends the framework to 23/5 trading. Filed as immediately effective.

rationale: Nasdaq rule filing amending MWCB Level 3 resumption timing in connection with the industry's 23-5 trading-hours expansion; structurally notable for market-wide halt handling but not a protocol/spec or cert change.
summary: Nasdaq proposes amending Equity 4, Rule 4121(b)(ii) to retain a 4:00 a.m. ET or later resumption time following a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker halt, even though the exchange may begin trading at 9:00 p.m. ET once 23-5 Trading is implemented. The change preserves the current post-Level 3 resumption behavior in the Pre-Market Hours session rather than aligning it with the expanded 9:00 p.m. ET start.

rationale: A Nasdaq rule filing eliminating duplicative information-circular requirements for UTP derivative securities and updating cross-references; it is a structural rule change but has no protocol, connectivity, or operational impact on options market-making infrastructure.

Rule filing amending Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker resumption mechanics in connection with the industry's 23/5 trading expansion; affects halt/resume logic that options market-making systems must handle, but is a structural rule change rather than a protocol or cert item.
summary: Nasdaq Texas is amending Equity 4 Rule 4121 so that after a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker halt, trading resumes at 7:00 a.m. ET under the industry's planned 23/5 schedule, with new overnight sessions running 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET beginning December 6, 2026. The change aligns Nasdaq Texas with other exchanges' uniform Level 3 MWCB rules; Nasdaq Texas itself does not intend to offer 23/5 trading at this time.

rationale: PHLX rule filing amending MWCB Level 3 halt resumption mechanics to accommodate the industry's 23/5 overnight trading expansion, directly affecting options market-making session handling and halt/resume logic.
summary: Nasdaq PHLX filed to amend Equity 4, Rule 3101 so that after a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker halt, trading resumes consistent with the industry's 23/5 trading expansion; several exchanges including Nasdaq intend to launch overnight sessions from 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET on December 6, 2026. PHLX itself does not intend to implement 23/5 trading at this time, but the uniform Level 3 MWCB rules are being modified across exchanges. Options market-making systems that model halt/resume behavior around the 8:00 a.m. ET resumption should track the coordinated rule changes.

rationale: Rule filing amending Cboe EDGX Rule 11.24(b)(2) to retain the 4 a.m. resumption time after a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker halt despite the shift to 23/5 trading hours. This is a structural rule change affecting halt/resumption logic that market-making systems must handle, tied to the December 2026 23x5 expansion.
summary: Cboe EDGX filed to amend Rule 11.24(b)(2) so that following a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker halt, trading resumes at 4:00 a.m. ET (start of the Early Trading Session) rather than at the 9:00 p.m. ET start of the 23/5 trading day. The change is tied to the exchange's 23x5 trading expansion, which takes effect in December 2026. Market-making systems that model session boundaries and MWCB resumption logic will need to account for the retained 4 a.m. resumption under the new 23-hour schedule.

rationale: This is a Nasdaq listing-rule operative-date change for a $5M Market Value of Listed Securities continued listing requirement, which is a corporate/listing matter unrelated to options market-making infrastructure, protocols, or connectivity.

SEC extension of the action deadline on MEMX's proposed rule change to list and trade securities event contracts on its options platform. This is a structurally notable market-structure development (a new product class on a US options exchange), but it is a procedural extension rather than a technical spec or cert item.
summary: The SEC has designated November 25, 2026 as the new deadline to approve, disapprove, or institute proceedings on MEMX's proposed rule change (SR-MEMX-2026-25) to adopt Chapter 30 governing listing and trading of securities event contracts on the Exchange's options platform. The original 45-day action deadline of October 11, 2026 was extended to allow further consideration of the filing and issues raised in comment.

rationale: Cboe EDGX is sunsetting its Last Sale Feed, a market data feed referenced in Rule 13.8(d), with the specific sunset date to be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days. This is a feed-product retirement affecting connectivity and data consumption for EDGX subscribers.
summary: Cboe EDGX proposes to sunset its Last Sale Feed, removing it from Rule 11.22(g) and eliminating all associated fees upon implementation. The specific sunset date will be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days of the filing. Subscribers currently receiving the Last Sale Feed will need to migrate to alternative feeds such as EDGX Top or EDGX Depth, which contain the same execution information plus top-of-book quotations.

rationale: Cboe EDGA is sunsetting its Last Sale Feed, a market data feed product change affecting connectivity and feed subscribers; the specific sunset date will be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days, so no explicit calendar deadline is present.
summary: Cboe EDGA proposes to sunset its Last Sale Feed (referenced in Rule 13.8(d)) and remove all associated fees, with the specific sunset date to be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days of the filing. The feed is redundant with EDGA Top and EDGA Depth, and subscribers can migrate to EDGA Top at no additional cost. Firms consuming the Last Sale Feed should plan migration to an alternative EDGA feed.

rationale: Rule filing amending Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker resumption mechanics to accommodate the industry's 23/5 overnight trading expansion, directly affecting halt/resume logic in trading systems. It is a structural rule change (MWCB) rather than a protocol or cert item.
summary: Cboe BYX proposes amending Rule 11.29(b)(2) so that after a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker halt, trading resumes consistent with the industry's 23/5 extended-hours regime; several exchanges including affiliate Cboe EDGX intend to launch overnight sessions from 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET starting December 6, 2026. The uniform Level 3 MWCB rules across SROs are being modified in tandem, changing the resumption time currently set at 7:00 a.m. ET the following trading day.

rationale: Cboe BZX is retiring the Last Sale Feed (Rule 11.22(g)) and removing associated fee-schedule entries; the sunset date will be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days of the filing. This is a feed-product retirement affecting connectivity/market-data consumers, though the exact cutover date is not yet specified.

The feed is deemed redundant since execution data is available via BZX Top and BZX Depth. The specific sunset date will be announced via Exchange Notice within 90 days after the filing is submitted to the SEC.

rationale: Amends the uniform Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker resumption rule to accommodate the industry's 23/5 overnight trading expansion, a structural rule change affecting halt/resume logic across US equities and options markets.
summary: Cboe EDGA filed to amend Rule 11.23(b)(2) governing resumption of trading after a Level 3 Market-Wide Circuit Breaker halt, in connection with the industry's move to 23/5 trading. Several exchanges, including affiliate EDGX, intend to launch overnight sessions from 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET starting December 6, 2026, which requires modifying the uniform Level 3 resumption rules (currently resume next trading day at 7:00 a.m. ET).

rationale: Amends Cboe BZX Rule 11.30(b)(2) governing resumption of trading after a Level 3 market-wide circuit breaker halt to accommodate the industry's 23/5 overnight trading expansion, with EDGX planning overnight sessions from 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET starting December 6, 2026. This is a structural rule filing affecting market-wide halt/resumption mechanics that options market-making infrastructure must handle.
summary: Cboe BZX filed to amend Rule 11.30(b)(2) so that after a Level 3 Market Decline halt, trading resumes consistent with the industry's 23/5 expansion; several exchanges including affiliate Cboe EDGX intend to launch overnight sessions from 9:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. ET on December 6, 2026. The change modifies the uniform MWCB resumption rules across SROs to account for extended hours, affecting how market-wide halt and resumption states are processed in overnight sessions.

rationale: SEC has instituted proceedings on NYSE Arca's proposal to extend cash settlement to up to 50 non-ETF FLEX Equity Options and change the selection metric to average daily notional value; this is a structural rule filing affecting options market-making and settlement mechanics.
summary: SEC instituted 19(b)(2)(B) proceedings on SR-NYSEARCA-2026-68, which would amend Rule 5.32-O(f)(3)(ii) to permit cash settlement for up to 50 non-ETF FLEX Equity Options meeting the same underlying criteria as the ETF FLEX cash-settlement program, and would change the selection of qualifying underlyings from highest average daily share volume to highest average daily notional value. The filing also correspondingly revises Rule 903G FLEX Equity Option position limits. Approval is now subject to further Commission analysis and comment.

rationale: SEC order instituting proceedings on an NYSE American rule filing that would expand cash settlement to up to 50 non-ETF FLEX Equity Options and change the selection metric to average daily notional value, with corresponding FLEX position-limit revisions. This is a structural, MM-affecting rule filing for a US options exchange, though it remains a pending proceeding rather than an imminent technical change.
summary: SEC has instituted proceedings to determine whether to approve or disapprove NYSE American's proposed amendment to Rules 903G and 906G, which would permit cash settlement for up to 50 non-ETF FLEX Equity Options meeting the same underlying-security criteria as the existing ETF FLEX cash settlement program. The filing also changes the selection metric, when more than 50 underlyings qualify, from highest average daily share volume to highest average daily notional value, and correspondingly revises FLEX Equity Option position limits under Rule 906G. The proposal was filed June 29, 2026 and published for comment July 7, 2026; the Commission is seeking additional comment on consistency with Section 6(b)(5).

rationale: This is a structural rule filing that directly changes Market-Maker quoting obligations on Cboe C2 by introducing a time-to-expiration tier to bid/ask differential requirements, which affects quoting logic and compliance for options market-making systems.
summary: Cboe C2 filed to amend Rule 5.52(c) to add a time-to-expiration tier to Market-Maker bid/ask differential requirements: a $5 maximum differential for options series expiring in 270 days or less, and a $15 maximum for series expiring in more than 270 days, conforming to Cboe Options Rule 5.52(c). The filing was immediately effective upon publication.

rationale: IEX is establishing listing standards for crypto-asset commodity-based trust options and position/exercise limits for IBIT ahead of its IEX Options launch on October 2, 2026, a new US options venue with new product coverage relevant to market-making infrastructure.
summary: IEX filed to amend Rules 20.120(i) and 20.130(g) to add generic listing and withdrawal criteria for options on Commodity-Based Trusts holding single or multiple crypto assets, and to set position and exercise limits for iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) under Rules 19.160 and 19.180. The changes precede the planned October 2, 2026 launch of IEX Options, which was approved September 18, 2025.

rationale: This is a structural rule filing that changes Market Maker quoting obligations on Cboe EDGX options, directly affecting market-making infrastructure compliance and quote-generation logic.
summary: Cboe EDGX proposes amending Rule 22.6(c) to introduce a time-to-expiration tier into Market Maker bid/ask differential requirements: a $5 maximum for options series expiring in 270 days or less, and a $15 maximum for series expiring in more than 270 days. This conforms EDGX to the approach already used by Cboe Options Rule 5.52(c) and similar provisions at ISE and Phlx. The filing is immediately effective, so quoting systems must enforce the new differential thresholds by expiration bucket.

MIAX PEARL rule filing amending equity risk controls (Limit Order Price Protection and Trading Collars) to define reference prices for the industry-wide move to 23/5 trading. This is a structural rule change affecting quoting/risk behavior, relevant to market-structure direction even though it is an equities-focused filing.
summary: MIAX PEARL filed to amend Exchange Rules 2614(a)(1)(ix) (Limit Order Price Protection) and 2618(b)(1) (Trading Collars) to specify reference prices under the upcoming 23-hours-per-day, 5-days-per-week trading expansion by other exchanges and the SIPs. The proposal limits the outside-RTH last trade reference to trades between 4:00 a.m.–9:30 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.–8:00 p.m. ET, preserving the current last-trade reference behavior. This is an immediate-effectiveness filing tied to the broader 23/5 market-structure shift.

rationale: Nasdaq rule filing amending Equity 2, Section 9 to require written clearing-member affirmation for Night Session (23-5) trades — a structural clearing/settlement obligation tied to the new overnight session, relevant to market-structure direction though not a protocol or connectivity change.
summary: Nasdaq proposes to amend Equity Rule 2, Section 9 so that a Member trading in the Night Session through another Member that is a clearing-agency member must have that Clearing Member affirm in writing (letter of authorization, guarantee, consent, or other acceptable agreement) that it assumes clearing and settlement responsibility for the designating Member's Night Session trades. The change is filed as immediately effective in connection with preparations for 23-5 overnight trading, and clearing firms requested the mechanism to control which correspondents may use their clearing services overnight. It does not alter existing clearing relationships outside the Night Session.
